newsitem.title: UK: Azlan plans Dutch buy, sets 3 for 10 rights.
newsitem.headline: Azlan plans Dutch buy, sets 3 for 10 rights.

text.p: British-based information technology training and support company Azlan Plc said on Tuesday it had agreed in principle to buy Dutch training group Akam BV for a maximum consideration of 29.6 million stg.
In parallel it said it was launching a three-for-10 rights issue priced at 620 pence per share intended to raise 48.5 million stg net.
Azlan also included its results for the six months to October 4. Its pretax profits rose by 36 percent to 6.0 milion stg, while earnings per share rose by 10 percent to 15.0 pence.
The company will pay an interim dividend of 1.3 pence per share, up from 1.2 pence a year ago.
The company said that since its flotation in 1993 it has pursued a strategy of building a pan-European business and now operates in 11 countries,
"The acquisition of Akam will substantially strengthen our network computing services busines," the statement quoted chief executive Christian Martin as saying.
"The rapid integration of Akam into the Group will enable us to increase product sales by introducing selected Azlan Group products to Akam's existing customer base.
"We expect the acquisition to be earnings enhancing within the first year and anticipate that it will lead to further improvements in the group's long term prospects," Martin added.
The rights issue is conditional on approval at an extraordinary general meeting of Azlan to be held on December 12, and on the acquisition agreement remaining in place.
